A sinusoidal signal is continuous and can take on any value within its amplitude range, which is a defining characteristic of an analog signal.  
Option (A) correctly states that it can have a number of values between the negative and positive peaks, meaning it is continuous in amplitude.  
The other options describe features of a sine wave but do not define why it is analog — for example, having positive and negative values or alternating signs does not inherently make it analog (a digital signal could represent those values discretely).  

Final answer: (A)
